title: China Freight Rates Split as EU Customs Bite Imports
metaDescription: China-Europe air rates fall 7% while belly hold cargo grows at Frankfurt. September trade surplus hits $133.5bn and chip exports jump 136%. What it means…
bottomLine: China to North Europe air rates fell 7% last week while transpacific air rose 3%, so your lane choice now decides your margin. The EU's abolished €150 customs exemption is showing up in the data, with China and Hong Kong imports at Frankfurt down 1.8% and 7.4% in September. China's September trade surplus hit $133.5 billion, which keeps tariff pressure from Brussels and Washington running hot into 2027 contract season.

stories.headline: China-Europe air rates drop 7% while transpacific holds firm
stories.tldr: China to North Europe air freight rates fell 7% week on week, while China to North America rose 3%, widening the gap between the two lanes.
stories.whatHappened:
Freightos data for the week to 13 October 2026 shows China to North Europe air prices down 7%, with China to North America up 3%. On ocean, Asia to US West Coast fell 2%, Asia to North Europe and US East Coast held level, and Asia to Mediterranean climbed 7% to $3,800 per FEU.

Houthi missile attacks on Riyadh airport since late last week shut down operations there, with disruption at other Saudi hubs. Freightos warns this raises the chance of renewed Red Sea strikes, even as carriers have added Asia-Europe Red Sea transits since June. Asia-Europe spot rates have fallen since July but remain above $3,000 per FEU, about 70% higher than a year ago, as 2027 tendering season begins.
stories.whyItMatters:
If you ship air freight into Europe, this is your window. A 7% weekly drop gives you room to renegotiate spot allocations or shift Q4 top-up volume onto European inbound. If you ship to the US, expect the opposite, with peak demand and Far East congestion holding rates near July levels.

On ocean, do not sign a 2027 annual contract at current benchmarks without pushing back. Rates are 70% above last year and carriers will use October GRIs to anchor negotiations, but newbuild deliveries and more Red Sea transits point to softer rates next year. If the Saudi escalation spreads, check which of your bookings transit Bab el-Mandeb.
stories.hotTake: Carriers want you to lock 2027 contracts at rates 70% above last year, and the October GRIs are theatre to make that number look normal. I would sign short, three to six months, and reprice in spring when the newbuilds hit the water. The Saudi escalation is the one thing that could prove me wrong, so keep one eye on Riyadh.
actions: Shift discretionary Q4 air freight for Europe into the next two weeks to capture the 7% rate drop
Refuse 2027 ocean contracts at current levels and counter with six-month terms
Audit your Asia-Europe bookings for Red Sea transits and price a Cape of Good Hope fallback

stories.headline: EU €150 exemption removal cuts China air imports at Frankfurt
stories.tldr: China imports at Frankfurt fell 1.8% and Hong Kong fell 7.4% in September after the EU abolished the €150 customs exemption in July.
stories.whatHappened:
Frankfurt Airport handled 174,773 tonnes of cargo in September 2026, up 2.5% year on year, with belly hold cargo up 6.6% to 72,500 tonnes and freighter tonnage flat at 102,200 tonnes. US traffic drove the growth, up 8.0%.

The airport directly linked weak Chinese and Hong Kong imports to the abolition of the EUR 150 customs exemption threshold in July and declining e-commerce shipments. Far East traffic grew 3.2% overall, but India rose 14.9%, Taiwan 19.3% and Japan 11.2%, so the growth came from outside China. On Far East routes, belly hold cargo rose 12.3% while freighter tonnage slipped 0.4%, helped by added passenger services to China.
stories.whyItMatters:
This is the first hard airport data showing what the end of the €150 exemption does to direct-to-consumer China shipping. If you run a low-value direct-ship model into the EU, your clearance cost per parcel went up in July and volumes are now visibly falling. If you import in bulk and clear as a normal importer, your position against the direct-ship platforms improved.

The belly hold shift matters for your rates. More passenger flights to China means more cheap belly capacity on Far East lanes, one reason China to Europe air rates are falling. If you fly goods into Germany, ask your forwarder for belly hold pricing before accepting freighter rates.
stories.hotTake: The de minimis crackdown was always going to show up in the data before it showed up in anyone's policy review, and here it is. Frankfurt is the EU's clearest scoreboard for China e-commerce air freight, and it says the low-value direct model is shrinking. Expect the platforms to reroute through bulk clearance and EU fulfilment.
actions: Recalculate your EU landed cost per parcel with post-July duty and clearance fees if you ship direct to consumer
Ask your forwarder to quote belly hold versus freighter rates on China to Germany lanes
Review whether bulk import into an EU fulfilment centre now beats direct shipping on cost

stories.headline: China posts $133.5bn September surplus, second highest on record
stories.tldr: China recorded a $133.5 billion trade surplus in September 2026, putting the full-year figure on track to beat 2025's record $1.19 trillion.
stories.whatHappened:
China's General Administration of Customs reported a $133.5 billion trade surplus for September 2026, the second-highest monthly figure on record after January 2025. The surplus with the US reached a 20-month high of $34.01 billion.

Chinese data shows total September goods trade of 5.16 trillion yuan, the first month above 5 trillion, up 27.5% year on year, with exports up 29.6% and imports up 24.6%. Analysts point to a weak renminbi and exporter tax breaks, which cost China's finance ministry about $318 billion in 2025, as drivers. Earlier in October, China agreed with the EU to halve its hybrid car sales in the bloc.
stories.whyItMatters:
A surplus this size is political fuel. Brussels is already angry about cheap Chinese vehicles, and a US trade deficit at a 20-month high hands tariff hawks a fresh argument. If you import from China into the US or EU, plan for more duty action, not less, through 2027. The EU hybrid deal shows Beijing will accept quotas and trim export support under pressure, and those rebate cuts raise factory export prices.

The weak renminbi works in your favour right now. Your dollar and euro buy more Chinese goods than they did, so if you have been putting off a price renegotiation with your factory, this is the moment. Export order books are full, so move quickly.
stories.hotTake: Everyone sourcing from China benefits from the weak yuan and the export tax breaks, and everyone will pay for it later through tariffs. That is the trade. I would bank the margin now, lock pricing for Q1 production, and assume at least one new duty measure lands on my category before mid-2027.
actions: Renegotiate factory pricing now while the weak renminbi pads your margin
Model a tariff scenario for your top SKUs into the US and EU before setting 2027 prices
Ask your suppliers whether their pricing assumes current export VAT rebates

stories.headline: China chip exports jump 136% in value on AI memory prices
stories.tldr: China's IC exports hit $45 billion in September, up 136% year on year in value, on a 1% rise in volume as memory prices surged.
stories.whatHappened:
China exported $45 billion of integrated circuits in September 2026, up 136% year on year, according to customs data released on 14 October. Unit volume rose 1% to 32.7 billion units, meaning higher prices drove almost all of the value growth amid a memory chip boom linked to AI demand. Growth for the first nine months ran at 108%.

Separately, Counterpoint Research projects Yangtze Memory Technologies, China's leading flash memory maker, will grow revenue six times faster than industry peers this year as it expands into server-related business ahead of a planned IPO. Server-related revenue was near zero in 2024 and could reach 39% of the company's total by 2028.
stories.whyItMatters:
If your products contain memory, and almost everything with a chip does, your component costs are rising. A 136% value jump on 1% volume growth is a price spike, and it flows into quotes for consumer electronics, smart home kit and anything with storage. Expect your next factory quote to carry a memory surcharge or a shorter price validity window.

Sellers who locked component pricing earlier this year hold an advantage into Q4. If you are quoting new products for 2027, build in higher memory costs rather than assuming prices normalise.
stories.hotTake: Memory is the new shipping container, a boring input that suddenly decides your margin. When a supplier gives you a quote valid for seven days instead of thirty, that is the memory market talking. I would pull forward any electronics production planned for Q1 and lock component pricing before the AI demand wave lifts prices again.
actions: Ask your electronics suppliers to itemise memory cost in their next quote
Pull forward Q1 2027 electronics production to lock current component pricing
Shorten your retail price validity assumptions for storage-heavy products

Frankfurt's September data is the first hard proof that killing the €150 exemption shrinks China e-commerce air imports
China's $133.5 billion September surplus makes new tariffs in 2027 more likely, not less
Chip export value up 136% on 1% volume growth means memory prices are doing to electronics quotes what freight did in 2021
Carriers want 2027 ocean contracts signed at rates 70% above last year, and the October GRIs are there to anchor you
Belly hold cargo is growing faster than freighters on China-Europe lanes, so ask for belly pricing before you accept a freighter quote
The Houthi attacks on Riyadh matter to your ocean bookings because they raise the odds of the Red Sea closing again
A weak yuan is padding your sourcing margin right now, and tariffs will take it back later
If your supplier's quote validity dropped from 30 days to 7, that is the memory market, not the supplier

faq.question: Are China to Europe air freight rates falling right now?
faq.answer: Yes. Freightos data for the week to 13 October 2026 shows China to North Europe air rates down 7% week on week, while China to North America rose 3%. Belly hold capacity on Far East routes is growing as airlines add passenger flights to China. If you have discretionary Q4 air volume for Europe, booking in the next two weeks captures the dip.

faq.question: What did the EU's removal of the €150 customs exemption do to imports?
faq.answer: The exemption ended in July 2026. September data from Frankfurt Airport shows imports from China down 1.8% year on year and Hong Kong down 7.4%, which the airport linked to the abolition and declining e-commerce shipments. Low-value direct-to-consumer parcels now carry duty and clearance costs they previously avoided, pushing sellers toward bulk import and EU-based fulfilment.

faq.question: Should I sign a 2027 ocean freight contract at current rates?
faq.answer: Push back first. Asia-Europe spot rates sit above $3,000 per FEU, about 70% higher than a year ago, and carriers are announcing October GRIs to anchor negotiations high. Newbuild deliveries in 2027 and rising Red Sea transits point to more capacity and softer rates. Shorter terms of three to six months let you reprice when that capacity arrives.

faq.question: Why are electronics quotes from China rising in late 2026?
faq.answer: Memory chip prices. China's IC exports rose 136% in value in September 2026 on a 1% rise in unit volume, so prices drove the increase amid AI-related demand. Anything with storage carries higher component costs. Expect shorter price validity from suppliers and lock component pricing for Q1 2027 production now.

faq.question: Do the Houthi attacks on Saudi airports affect my shipments?
faq.answer: Missile attacks since late last week shut down Riyadh airport and disrupted other Saudi hubs, raising the chance of renewed Red Sea strikes on shipping. Carriers have increased Asia-Europe Red Sea transits since June, so some bookings may route through Bab el-Mandeb. Check your routings and price a Cape of Good Hope alternative, which adds roughly 10 to 14 days.
